h1: Water is leaking around a cylinder
title: Water is leaking around a cylinder | G3 Cylinder Help
description: Understand water is leaking around a cylinder. Distinguish the symptom, gather useful details and arrange competent cylinder assessment in London.
answer: Identify whether water comes from a connection, valve, discharge route or the cylinder vessel. Those findings lead to different repair decisions.

sections.heading: What this symptom can mean
paragraphs: A wet cupboard does not establish a leaking vessel. Water can track from a nearby fitting or connected appliance. Electrical equipment, damaged flooring and active leaks need consideration before an ordinary service visit.

sections.heading: Information to gather safely
paragraphs: Provide a wide photograph and describe the visible origin without disturbing fittings. Keep clear of wet electrical controls; a vessel leak should not be confused with normal safety discharge through its intended route.

sections.heading: How the enquiry becomes an investigation
paragraphs: The cylinder make, full model and heating arrangement should be identified first. The same visible symptom can arise from different causes, and a relief device may be protecting the system rather than creating the original problem. Component testing and any repair belong to a person competent for the work.

sections.heading: Discuss the appropriate next step
paragraphs: Call 020 7205 4433 with the postcode, symptom history and any previous service findings. The enquiry establishes the proposed assessment and availability. Do not use this guide as a substitute for the actual appliance safety instructions or an on-site diagnosis.

faqs.question: Can water beside a cylinder come from something other than the vessel?
faqs.answer: Yes. Connections, valves, discharge and nearby pipework can leak; the origin must be traced before recommending a replacement cylinder.
